challenge.description: A security audit revealed that the API gateway lacks proper authentication controls, exposing model endpoints to unauthorized access. #automation_alex# argues for keeping the gateway in a manual state to avoid disrupting the current deployment pipeline, while #requirements_reuben# insists on a fully governed state to ensure compliance and security.

output.content: I am not touching the gateway automation until the pipeline is rock solid. My primary duty is keeping the deployment flow stable for the team. If we automate the authentication layer now, we risk breaking the integration tests that currently pass every night. I will not approve any changes to the gateway configuration if they introduce instability into the CI/CD chain. The current manual setup is fragile but it works without interrupting the build cycle. I refuse to accept any configuration change that might cause a single failed deployment during the next sprint. The stability of the pipeline is my non-negotiable requirement for any infrastructure work I sign off on.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly refuses to approve changes or accept instability, establishing a hard line that crossing means refusal of their sign-off.
